notes: Iteration 3 reviewed b8ec047..HEAD: 6e448c2 (taxonomy/) and 7ada6a0 (test report). Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED for sequencing only; the diff itself is clean and no rework is requested.

DEFECT 2 verified empirically, not by source reading: loading the real cub200.csv and coco_animals.csv through the shipped code yields chuck_wills_widow, arctic_tern, brewers_blackbird and forsters_tern; all 210 labels across both tables satisfy LABEL_RE, none begins with a digit, none collides with RESERVED_LABELS; cub_key_from_dirname('022.Chuck_will_Widow') -> 'chuck_will_widow' (a key, never a directory).

The key/label split is the right shape: CUB's own misspelling 141.Artic_Tern is preserved in the key because that is what the dataset is keyed by, while the folder is corrected to arctic_tern from the authoritative display name.
_reject_raw_dataset_id turns a future digit-prefixed regression into a load-time ConfigError (exit 3) rather than a directory on disk, applied to both key and label.

load_table's duplicate-LABEL check is the most valuable validation in the file: two display names slugifying onto one directory would silently merge two species into one folder and no later stage could detect it.

I7 fail-loud is honoured: TaxonTable.__getitem__ (and label_for/common_for/rank_for through it) raises ConfigError naming the file and the fix; slug() raises rather than returning a sanitized guess; only `scientific`, a genuinely optional field, is allowed to be absent and is stored as None.

No min_box_area and no absolute area floor anywhere in code or config. git grep over ten spellings returns one hit outside docs -- config.py:14, a docstring asserting no such knob exists. dominance_ratio remains the only size gate, still guarded executably by the 6 parametrised CLI tests.

The .gitignore `data/` -> `/data/` anchoring plus the hatchling `artifacts` entry is a real data-loss catch: the unanchored pattern matched src/animal_classifier/taxonomy/data/, and hatchling honours VCS ignore files, so the CSVs would have been dropped from both `git add -A` and the wheel with no local reproduction.
No write to the SD-card tree is introduced by this diff; taxonomy/ is pure in-package data loading.
Test hygiene clean: 7 passed / exit 0 with verbatim captured output, no unit tests, no test outside tests/e2e/, testpaths pinned to tests/e2e, nothing deleted to make the suite green.

F8 (non-blocking) -- merged()'s docstring sentence 'disjoint apart from nothing at all' is garbled, and the merge is order-dependent: cub200() overwrites coco_animals(), so a future CUB row keyed `bird` would silently shadow COCO's. No collision today (merged size 210 = 10 + 200).

F9 (non-blocking) -- find_by_common/find_by_scientific index with setdefault, so a duplicate silently keeps the first row while duplicate keys and labels raise. Reachable for `scientific`, where coarser-rank rows can legitimately share a genus or family name.
F10 (non-blocking) -- TaxonTable's _by_common/_by_scientific are dataclass fields, so the underscore names appear in the constructor signature.

F11 (non-blocking) -- Taxon.scientific is typed str | None while the CSV column is empty-string; the conversion sits in one place (`scientific or None`). Document the invariant before the GUI serializers land in chunks 20-22.

F12 (non-blocking, self-resolving at chunk 18) -- taxonomy/ has no e2e coverage at this commit; neither catalog.py nor taxonomy/labels.py is reachable from a --help invocation. Correctness rests on this review's spot-check and PROGRESS.md's ad-hoc runs. Same shape as F7.

F13 (non-blocking) -- the claim that cub200.csv's 200 keys match CUB_200_2011.tgz's classes.txt exactly and in order rests on an ad-hoc run recorded in PROGRESS.md. Chunks 15-18 should assert it where the artifact's label list loads, since a silent reordering would mislabel every bird.
